auditFocus: an .unwrap()/.expect() on a Result or Option built from untrusted or fallible external input (a network response, a file read, a parsed argument) instead of propagating with ?
an unsafe block with no # Safety doc comment stating the invariants the caller must uphold, or one wider than the specific operation that requires it
a borrow-checker conflict worked around with an unnecessary .clone() instead of restructuring ownership, splitting borrows, or using a reference
a blocking call (std::thread::sleep, a synchronous file/network read, a std::sync::Mutex held across an .await) inside an async fn instead of the async equivalent or spawn_blocking
an integer operation on untrusted input with no overflow/bounds check (raw arithmetic or indexing instead of checked_add/get/saturating_* where the value could be attacker-influenced)
a custom error type that loses the underlying cause instead of using #[source]/#[from] (thiserror) or .context() (anyhow) to preserve it
fixGuardrails: Never silence a clippy finding with a blanket #[allow(clippy::all)] or a lint-level allow instead of fixing the root cause.
Never add .unwrap()/.expect() to make a type error or a Result mismatch disappear; propagate with ? or handle the error explicitly.
Never bump the edition or MSRV in Cargo.toml just to make an error disappear without understanding why it changed.
Never delete or skip a failing test to reach a green build.
Never widen an unsafe block or drop a # Safety comment to silence a compiler or clippy complaint about it.
